lines.caption: A new Rayfin app comes with more than a hundred files. What are they all for?
Your code lives in three packages… and one small file tells Fabric what to run.
Hi, I'm Ray! Welcome back to Learn Rayfin with Ray.

lines.said: [excited] Today: what each package does, what rayfin dot yaml turns on, and the building blocks your app can grow. Let's dive in!
lines.caption: Today: what each package does, what rayfin.yml turns on, and the building blocks your app can grow. Let's dive in!
Your new app is an npm workspace: one project that holds a few packages, each with its own job.
The frontend package is your website: React and Vite, sign-in, and the pages people see.
The data package holds your entities, the classes from lesson one, and registers each one in its schema.
The shared package holds the types that your frontend, your data and your functions all agree on.
And when your app needs functions, a functions package joins them.

lines.said: Beside the packages sits the rayfin folder, and in it, rayfin dot yaml: your backend's configuration.
lines.caption: Beside the packages sits the rayfin folder, and in it, rayfin.yml: your backend's configuration.
It lists your app's services, and rayfin dev and rayfin up sync it to Fabric.
Auth turns on sign-in with Microsoft Entra ID, through Fabric.
Static hosting serves your frontend. Its asset access starts protected, so pages load only after sign-in.
Data is your database. It starts off, and turns on when your app needs records of its own.
Functions and storage are services too. Connectors and secrets each get a list of their own.
rayfin dev and rayfin up also write two files of their own into the rayfin folder.

lines.said: dot env holds values your frontend needs, like your backend's address.
lines.caption: .env holds values your frontend needs, like your backend's address.

lines.said: And dot deployments dot JSON records each place you deployed: its workspace, its Fabric app and its address.
lines.caption: And.deployments.json records each place you deployed: its workspace, its Fabric app and its address.

lines.said: Both are about where you deployed, not what you built, so git leaves them out. rayfin dot yaml is the one you commit.
lines.caption: Both are about where you deployed, not what you built, so git leaves them out. rayfin.yml is the one you commit.
Time for a deep dive! What does your app become, inside Fabric?
rayfin up packages your project and sets it up as a Fabric app, inside your organization's tenant.
Your frontend is served as static content. Behind it, a web service and Data API Builder sit in front of a SQL database.
Functions run beside them, on the server, and blob storage holds your app's files.
Sign-in is built in, too. Fabric brokers it, so people sign in with the Microsoft Entra account they already use for Fabric.
There's no identity provider to run, and no Entra app of your own for a tenant admin to approve.
Connectors reach outside the app, to data already in Fabric: a warehouse, a SQL database, a Lakehouse SQL endpoint, or a semantic model.
And functions reach the rest: Microsoft resources, with the app's own identity, and any web API, with a secret.

lines.said: [proudly] And rayfin dot yaml decides which of these pieces your app gets.
lines.caption: And rayfin.yml decides which of these pieces your app gets.
Here's the same tour in Fabricator. The Code view shows your project's files, packages and all.

lines.caption: And Blueprint draws your app from rayfin.yml and your code: Website, Sign-in, Database, File storage, Connectors, Functions and Secrets.
Lines show what each piece connects to, and which identity it uses.
Pop quiz! Which file records where you deployed, and stays out of git?

lines.said: A, dot deployments dot JSON. B, rayfin dot yaml. Or C, package dot JSON.
lines.caption: A,.deployments.json. B, rayfin.yml. Or C, package.json.
Pause the video, and guess…

lines.said: [cheering] It's A, dot deployments dot JSON! It's about where you deployed, so git leaves it out. You commit rayfin dot yaml.
lines.caption: It's A,.deployments.json! It's about where you deployed, so git leaves it out. You commit rayfin.yml.

lines.said: Let's recap. Your code lives in packages: frontend, data and shared. rayfin dot yaml lists your services. And Fabric runs them all as one Fabric app.
